title: Changing the Board Docket and Advancement on the Docket in Decision Reviews and Appeals
content:
## Board appeals in Decision Reviews and Appeals — moving between dockets and advancement on the docket

**1. The rule.** A Board appellant may move to another docket within 60 days after the Board received the notice of disagreement or within one year of the decision notice, whichever is later, and only before any evidence or testimony has been submitted on the current docket. An appeal is advanced on the docket when the appellant is 75 or older or shows one of the grounds of serious illness, severe financial hardship or other sufficient cause; advancement does not change the docket.

**2. The period for a docket switch.** Two periods are compared, and the one that ends later governs:

- 60 days after the Board received the notice of disagreement; and
- one year of the decision notice.

The appellant may move to another docket within whichever of the two periods ends later.

**3. The evidence condition.** The switch is available only before any evidence or testimony has been submitted on the current docket. Once evidence or testimony has been submitted there, the switch is no longer available, even within the period.

**4. Combinations**

| Within the period (whichever of the two ends later) | Evidence or testimony already submitted on the current docket | Docket switch |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | May move to another docket |
| Yes | Yes | Not available |
| No | No | Not available |
| No | Yes | Not available |

**5. Hypothetical illustrations of the period**

- The Board receives the notice of disagreement in the second month after the decision notice. The 60 days after that receipt end well before one year from the decision notice, so the one-year period from the decision notice governs.
- The Board receives the notice of disagreement in the twelfth month after the decision notice. The 60 days after that receipt end after one year from the decision notice, so the 60-day period after receipt governs.

**6. What the record shows.** A move to another docket is recorded on the appeal as its new docket, with the hearing type where the new docket is the Hearing Docket and no hearing type otherwise. Advancement is recorded on the appeal as advanced on the docket.

**7. Advancement on the docket.** An appeal is advanced on the docket when either holds:

- the appellant is 75 years of age or older; or
- the appellant shows serious illness, severe financial hardship or other sufficient cause.

Hypothetical: an appellant aged 75 is advanced on the age ground; an appellant aged 74 who shows serious illness is advanced on that ground. In either case the appeal stays on the docket it was on: advancement does not change the docket.
